\begin{lemma}[Semantics of the rejection state]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ups_rej}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ups_rej}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.PSem.congr, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.rej, Complexity.LogProg.UPS, Complexity.LogProg.UReg, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.Le, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.reg}
\difficulty{1}
Let $x$ be a finite bit string, $B$ a natural-number bound, $\sigma$ a register state,
and $q$ a rational number. If every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$ and $q=0$, then
the universal probabilistic program started in the rejection state with register state
$\sigma$ has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Unary input initialization]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ups_unary}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ups_unary}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.PSem.call_neg, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.call_pos, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.inc, Complexity.LogProg.UPS, Complexity.LogProg.UPS.of_eq, Complexity.LogProg.UReg, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.Le, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.reg, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.v_0, Complexity.LogProg.pathOr_bit, Complexity.LogProg.ups_rej, Complexity.UnaryRest, Complexity.lt_of_getD_true}
\difficulty{6}
Let $x$ be a Boolean word, $B$ a natural number, $q$ a rational number, $d$ a natural
number, and $\sigma$ a register state with fields $p,n,a,b,cur,t,tmp,st,nx,q_{\mathrm{reg}},L,u,w,e,f$.
Suppose $|x|-\sigma.p=d$, every field of $\sigma$ is at most $B$,
$2|x|+2\le B$, $\sigma.p=2\sigma.n$, and $\sigma.p\le |x|$. For every $n\prime\ge\sigma.n$
whose unary suffix consists of aligned $11$ pairs from index $\sigma.n$ through $n\prime-1$,
followed by the terminator pair $01$, suppose the program from label $m0$ and the state
obtained by setting $p=2n\prime+2$ and $n=n\prime$ has acceptance probability $q$.
If there is no such $n\prime$, suppose $q=0$. Then the program from label $u0$ and state
\sigma has acceptance probability $q$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Matrix-checking program semantics]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ups_mat}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ups_mat}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.PSem.call_neg, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.call_pos, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.clr, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.inc, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jeq_neg, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jeq_pos, Complexity.LogProg.UPS, Complexity.LogProg.UPS.of_eq, Complexity.LogProg.UReg, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.Le, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.reg, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.v_0, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.v_1, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.v_2, Complexity.LogProg.pathOr_bit, Complexity.LogProg.pathOr_len, Complexity.LogProg.ups_rej, Complexity.MatRest, Complexity.div_eq_self_iff, Complexity.divmod_succ, Complexity.lt_of_getD_true}
\difficulty{7}
Let $x$ be a finite bit string, $B$ a natural number, $q$ a rational number, $i,dd$
natural numbers, and $\sigma$ a register state. Suppose $\sigma.n^2-i=dd$, every
register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$, $2|x|+2\le B$, $\sigma.n\le |x|$,
$\sigma.p=2\sigma.n+2+2i$, $\sigma.a=\lfloor i/\sigma.n\rfloor$,
$\sigma.b=i\bmod\sigma.n$, and $i\le\sigma.n^2$. If the matrix-rest condition holds for
$x,\sigma.n,i$, then the universal probabilistic program started at the matrix-checking
site with register state obtained from $\sigma$ by setting
$p=2\sigma.n+2+2\sigma.n^2+2$, $a=\sigma.n$, and $b=0$ has acceptance probability $q$.
If that condition fails, then $q=0$. In either case, the program started at its
multiplication-and-checking entry site with register state $\sigma$ has probabilistic
semantics with acceptance probability $q$; the semantics also require termination along
every sequence of choices and the stated register bound throughout the run.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Column symmetry check]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ups_ycol}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ups_ycol}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.PSem.call_neg, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.call_pos, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.inc, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jeq_neg, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jeq_pos, Complexity.LogProg.UPS, Complexity.LogProg.UPS.of_eq, Complexity.LogProg.UReg, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.Le, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.reg, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.v_0, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.v_11, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.v_12, Complexity.LogProg.ixCol, Complexity.LogProg.ixEx, Complexity.LogProg.ixRow, Complexity.LogProg.pathOr_bit, Complexity.LogProg.ups_index, Complexity.LogProg.ups_rej, Complexity.pathEdge, Complexity.rowMajor_lt}
\difficulty{6}
Let $x$ be a Boolean word, $B$ a natural number, and $q$ a rational number. Suppose
$\sigma.n-\sigma.w=dd$, every field of the register state $\sigma$ is at most $B$,
$2\sigma.n+2+2\sigma.n^2\le B$, $\sigma.u<\sigma.n$, and $\sigma.w\le\sigma.n$. If the
encoded adjacency relation is symmetric between row $\sigma.u$ and every column $w'$
with $\sigma.w\le w'<\sigma.n$, then for all $p,a,b\le B$, the program at state $yn$
with $w$ reset to $\sigma.n$ and $p,a,b$ set to those values has probabilistic semantics
with acceptance probability $q$. If this column-symmetry condition does not hold, then
$q=0$ and the program at state $y2$ with register state $\sigma$ has probabilistic
semantics with acceptance probability $q$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Row symmetry transfer]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ups_yrow}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ups_yrow}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.PSem.clr, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.inc, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jeq_neg, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jeq_pos, Complexity.LogProg.UPS, Complexity.LogProg.UPS.of_eq, Complexity.LogProg.UReg, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.Le, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.reg, Complexity.LogProg.ups_ycol, Complexity.pathEdge}
\difficulty{6}
Let $x$ be a Boolean word, $B$ a natural number, and $q$ a rational number. Suppose
$\sigma$ is a register state and $dd$ is a natural number such that
$\sigma.n-\sigma.u=dd$, each register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$,
$2\sigma.n+2+2\sigma.n^2\le B$, and $\sigma.u\le\sigma.n$. If every encoded edge from a
row $u'$ with $\sigma.u\le u'<\sigma.n$ to a column $w'<\sigma.n$ is present exactly
when the reverse edge is present, then for all $p,a,b,w\le B$, the probabilistic
semantics of the program from state $s0$, with $u$ set to $\sigma.n$ and $w,p,a,b$ set
to those values, has acceptance probability $q$. If this row-symmetry condition fails
and $q=0$, then the program from state $y0$ and register state $\sigma$ has
probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$.
\end{lemma}
